'''René Andre Carmona''' (born August 6, 1947) is a French [[mathematician]] and professor at [[Princeton University]] who is known for developing a [[probabilistic model|probabilistic approach]] for [[mean field games]]. He is a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], the [[American Mathematical Society]] and the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].

==Education==
Carmona earned his undergraduate degree from the [[Aix-Marseille University]] in 1968 and would receive his Ph.D. from the same university in 1977. His thesis, ''Contribution à l'étude des mesures gaussiennes dans les espaces de Banach'', was supervised by [[Leonard Gross]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy | id= 31313 | name= René A Carmon}}</ref>

==Career==
Carmona's first academic job was at the [[Aix-Marseille University]] after he completed his Ph.D. He moved from [[Cornell University]] to [[Princeton University]] before taking a job as an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI) in 1981. Carmona became a full professor by 1984 and was named a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] the following year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Honored IMS Fellows |url=https://imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/ |website=imstat.org |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |access-date=11 September 2025 |language=en |archive-date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416083537/https://www.imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He stayed at UCI until 1995 when he accepted a professorship at Princeton.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bio & CV René Carmona |url=https://carmona.princeton.edu/maineducation.html |website=carmona.princeton.edu |access-date=11 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Carmona and {{ill|François Delarue|fr|François Delarue (mathématicien)}} were awarded the [[Joseph L. Doob Prize]] by the [[American Mathematical Society]] for their two volume series ''Probabilistic Theory of Mean Field Games with Applications''.<ref>{{cite web |title=René Carmona and François Delarue to Receive the 2020 Joseph L. Doob Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=5596 |website=www.ams.org |publisher=American Mathematical Society |date=November 4, 2019}}</ref> The books were published in 2018 by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] as part of the ''Probability Theory and Stochastic Modeling'' series.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Carmona |first1=René |last2=Delarue |first2=François |title=Probabilistic Theory of Mean Field Games with Applications I |series=Probability Theory and Stochastic Modelling |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-58920-6 |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-58920-6 |date=2018 |volume=83 |isbn=978-3-319-56437-1 }}</ref> The books contain the motivation and background for understanding the probabilistic model for [[mean field games]] that Carmona and Delarue spent the last decade researching.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fouque |first1=Jean-Pierre |title=Probabilistic Theory of Mean Field Games, Volumes I & II |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=1 June 2020 |volume=67 |issue=6 |pages=855–859 |doi=10.1090/noti2089  |doi-access=free|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/202006/rnoti-p855.pdf |publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>
